checks.what: afsharid-iran gain from mughal-empire, Jan 1740 (bridging for May 1739). Page: infobox 'Nader Shah annexes all lands west of the Indus river'; 'Nader and his Afsharid troops left Delhi on 16 May 1739'; 'he ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus ... to Muhammad Shah'. The date is a year-boundary bridge the brief forces, since the brief keeps each file to its own window; the cause is p1730-p1739, where the Mughal loss of May 1739 pairs with the Sindh-only afsharid-iran/ledger/12. The region (Afghanistan + K.P. + F.A.T.A. + Baluchistan + Pakistani Punjab minus an Indus polygon, intersected with Cliopatria Afsharid 1741) resolves to 3,581 cells, but a gain takes only what the counterpart holds. In the trial it moves 765 Mughal cells: Baluchistan 315, Punjab west of the Indus 106 (D.G. Khan, Rajanpur, Isakhel), K.P. 90, F.A.T.A. 73, Paktika 69, Zabul 66, Uruzgan 24, Khost 12 and others. Only 1 of the K.P./F.A.T.A./Punjab cells lies east of the Indus line (Haripur, Hazara), so the region holds no more than the page's land. Effect: mughal-empire_1740 now drops 421 cells instead of 1,186; afsharid-iran_1741 adds 418 instead of 1,183. The cells stay Afsharid through 1743, and 1744 drops 44 of them (Punjab 26, K.P. 18) as before, by afsharid-iran_1744. 1747-1749 is unchanged in kind (Durrani split, ledger/29). No new conflict.

duchy-of-courland gain from nobody, Jan 1740. Page: status 'Vassal state of ... Poland-Lithuania (1569-1795)'; 'incorporated into the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth in 1726'; Biron appointed duke 1737, exiled 1741; Louis Ernest chosen 27 June 1741 and deposed after the coup of 6 December 1741; Courland 'incorporated into the Russian Empire' with the final document of 24 October 1795. The page names no Russian annexation and no territorial loss between 1700 and 1795; it says Russia took Swedish Livonia, not Courland. The region is Cliopatria Duchy of Courland 1740: 122 cells, all of Latvia south and west of the Daugava (Ventspils, Kuldiga, Talsi, Saldus, Jelgava, Bauska, Ilukste/Selonia). That is about 30,700 km2 against the infobox's 27,290, and in line with the dossier's own 1734 keyframe. In the trial all 122 cells are nobody's on 1 Jan 1740 and the duchy's (vassal of polish-lithuanian-commonwealth) from 1740 to 1749; the p1750 anchor has 126 vassal cells. No conflict with Russia or anyone else. data/patches/p1750-p1759.json events/0 duplicates the gain and will now find nothing to take, which does no harm. The p1720-p1739 hole remains for those windows.

mughal-empire_1741 (1741-1743). The override is the dossier's correction unchanged plus (Cliopatria Afsharid 1741 ∩ India). Page: 'he ceded back all territories to the east of the Indus, which he had overrun, to Muhammad Shah'. The addition is 432 cells: Haryana 148, Indian Punjab 136, west UP 72, north Rajasthan 56 (Ganganagar to Jhunjhunu), Himachal 8, Delhi 5, Uttarakhand 5, Chandigarh 1, J&K 1. Of these, 427 were Mughal on 1 Jan 1740 and stay Mughal 1741-1749 in the trial, so the Delhi-heartland hole of 1741-1743 is closed (snap: 477 removed -> 50). The other 5 cells (Haridwar/Roorkee plain, 29.7-30.0 N, 77.9-78.1 E) are garhwal-kingdom's. They fall inside the dossier's fx-10 'Garhwal' cut, which the added clause bypasses, so they raise a 5-cell conflict that Garhwal wins by the size rule. The map is unchanged, and those plains were arguably Mughal (Saharanpur), so I left them. Nothing else is added or taken.

ottoman-empire_1744 (1744-1747). The override is the dossier's correction (Cliopatria 1744 without Azov) plus (Ottoman 1741 ∩ Ottoman 1748, without Azov). Page: Nader 'captured Kirkuk, Erbil and besieged Mosul on 14 September 1743'; 'The siege lasted for 40 days'; 'The Pasha of Mosul ... successfully defended Mosul'; territorial changes 'Status quo ante bellum'; Kerden, 4 September 1746: 'The boundaries were unchanged'. The page never says Sulaymaniyah or Hakkari were taken. The addition is 171 cells: Sulaymaniyah 64, Arbil 48, Kirkuk 20, Ninawa 19, Hakkari 7, Diyala 4, 6 Iranian border cells and 3 others. All 171 were already held at the end of 1743 (Ottoman 165, mamluk-iraq 6), so the override takes no new land. It stops the 1744 snap dropping 97 cells to nobody. Published: nobody's 1744-1747 and Ottoman again in 1748. Trial: Ottoman throughout, with the ottoman_1744 and _1748 snaps now empty. The Kirkuk/Erbil/Kars contest (afsharid-iran/ledger/17 to /21, 1743-1746) still applies. The mamluk-iraq/ottoman R2 conflict rises 730 -> 736 cells in 1744, which Mamluk Iraq wins, so the map is unchanged.

mughal-empire_1744 (1744-1747). The override is the dossier's correction unchanged plus the Pakistani Punjab, Islamabad and AJK east of the Indus, plus (Cliopatria Afsharid 1741 ∩ India). The page supports it: Shah Nawaz Khan was 'the Mughal governor of Punjab' when the Afghans seized Peshawar (1747); 'battle of Lahore on 11 January' 1748; 'In November 1748, Ahmad Shah began his second invasion', and Moin-ul-Mulk, 'the new governor of Punjab', ceded the revenues of Gujrat, Aurangabad, Sialkot and Pasrur; 'The Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah signed the treaty on 3 April 1752, ending Mughal rule in Punjab'. So the Punjab was Mughal in 1744-1747. All 284 added cells are inside the 1741 shape. Trial: 279 are Mughal from 1743 to 1747 (published: nobody's 1744-1747), and in 1748-1749 217 stay Mughal (published: 275 nobody's). The other 5 are the same Garhwal-held Haridwar cells as in keyframe_overrides/0, where Garhwal wins by size, so nothing changes on the map. The snap goes from 339 added / 134 removed to 57 / 0. No cells are taken from any other state.
